public_rationale: The S-1 filed on 2026-10-26 has financial statements that stop at June 30, 2026. Q3 revenue is left blank and given only as a multiple of an earlier quarter (e1). Some Q3 operating metrics do appear, but the Q3 financials are missing, so 'the majority' is a fair description. The four non-cancellable deals disclosed (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Broadcom) add up to $430.6 billion, which is over $430 billion (e3). Most of that capacity, and $321.4 billion of leases not yet begun, starts from 2026 to 2028, mostly 2027 (e3, e4). Implied Q3 growth was about 45-48% over Q2, down from 144% in Q2, and Q3 was the first quarter to add fewer dollars than the one before (e2). The jab about Anthropic being 'so confident' is sarcasm and is not graded.
limitations: Relies on secondary readings of the S-1 because the SEC page could not be read.
'Begin to kick in' is loose. Some cloud commitments are already being paid.
The Q3 growth figure is derived from a rounded multiple in the filing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic left the majority of its Q3 2026 numbers out of its S-1, reporting Q2 just before over $430 billion in non-cancellable compute commitments begin to kick in and its growth begins to slow.
conditions: majority of its third quarter numbers

statement.excerpt: Anthropic is so confident in its growth trajectory that it left out the majority of its third quarter 2026 numbers from its S-1, reporting a second quarter before over $430 billion in non-cancellable compute commitments begin to kick in and its growth begins to slow.

from_speaker: left out the majority of its third quarter 2026 numbers from its S-1
before over $430 billion in non-cancellable compute commitments begin to kick in
and its growth begins to slow
our_interpretation: 'So confident in its growth trajectory' is sarcasm about motive and is not graded.

'Left out the majority of Q3 numbers' holds if the S-1's financial statements stop at June 30, 2026 and Q3 dollar figures (such as revenue) are blank or missing, even if a few Q3 operating metrics appear.
'Over $430 billion in non-cancellable compute commitments' is checked against the non-cancellable compute deals disclosed in the S-1.
'Begin to kick in' holds if most of that committed capacity or payments start after the reported period, from late 2026 to 2028.
'Growth begins to slow' holds if Q3 2026 revenue growth was below Q2's growth rate, or if the filing says growth will decline.
criteria.support_condition: The S-1 statements end at Q2 2026 with Q3 financials blank. Its non-cancellable compute deals total more than $430 billion, with most capacity starting from 2027. Q3 growth was slower than Q2's, or the filing warns that growth will slow.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The S-1 includes full Q3 2026 financial statements, or non-cancellable commitments are well under $430 billion, or most commitments were already running by Q2, or Q3 growth matched or beat Q2.

evidence.explanation: Shows the S-1 financial statements stop at Q2 and the Q3 revenue figure is blank, given only as a multiple. This matches 'left out the majority of its Q3 numbers'.

evidence.excerpt: That is growth of about 45 to 48 percent on the second quarter, and about $5.2 billion to $5.6 billion added, the first quarter in the series to add fewer dollars than the one before.
evidence.locator: section 'The quarters, and the one in ratio form', paragraph 4
evidence.explanation: Q3 growth of about 45-48% compares with 144.2% in Q2 (same source), and Q3 added fewer dollars than Q2. Growth began to slow right after the last reported quarter.

evidence.excerpt: $114.5bn to Google through July 2033, $110bn to Amazon through April 2036 and $44.9bn to Microsoft through May 2033, “regardless of actual usage”. It has also committed to $161.2bn in five-year equipment leases with Broadcom, excluding interest. Neither party can cancel the leases, and most of the capacity is due to come online from 2027.
evidence.explanation: The four non-cancellable deals sum to $430.6 billion, which is over $430 billion. The largest, Broadcom, mostly comes online from 2027, so the commitments start after the reported quarter.

evidence.excerpt: At the end of June, it had signed $321.4bn of compute and infrastructure leases that had yet to begin, up from $50.2bn six months earlier, and they are due to start between 2026 and 2028.
evidence.explanation: Shows that a large share of committed compute had not yet started as of the last reported quarter and runs from 2026 to 2028. This supports 'before ... begin to kick in'.
